summary: I encodes the material's change of state; II adds a causer and an object, often suffixed. JTM 1.1/78 and 94/229–230 directly contrast the two stems in the same procedure.
Infectum-wa occurs in both stems. The inherited I example is not evidence for chewing and not an unmarked Infectum; the inherited II hand-crumbling example illustrates II.2.

II Detransitive Part. Pass. describes a melted result; mfašro also occurs in a description of the resulting butter product (94/196). This compositional material-state expression does not require a new lexical idiom.
gəmfašaṇṇo at MAC NE Interview 2/221 may reflect r+n assimilation. Keep the emphatic source spelling and the edition's 'tin', while asking whether riṣaṣ denotes lead.
This sample supplies no new evidence for I.2 chewing. It does not resolve the inherited question about splitting the root historically; retain both stems and all inherited sense numbers.

Round 1’s I.1 widening to sich auflösen already accommodates material dissolution and remains unchanged. Jan adds repeated social-identity uses; the explicit red-drop-in-water comparison at Jan 4.I/514 secures the figurative link.

I has affected material/community as subject; II has an external causer and material/community object. The political passages use mafšər- beside inherited mfašər-; morphology alone here cannot establish a separate III.

The wax token fəšrinawo u šamʕo at Jan 2.5/1574 appears transitive but lacks expected m-. It is insufficient to publish a new transitive I sense; reduced II, omitted syntax or source irregularity remain possible.

Round 1 already moved the misfiled I dissolution example to Infectum-wa sense 1 and assigned the II hand-crumbling example to sense 2. Those corrections are retained in the displayed counts, not repeated as round 2 proposals.
The inherited historical question about splitting roots is unresolved by Jan’s literal/figurative melting examples.
Does fšr in the lime passages mean dissolution, slaking, softening or disintegration? The broadened gloss avoids asserting heat-driven melting.
Confirm the source relationship between MlfI_Houses2/84 and MAC Ishaq Material culture/81 before replacing any citation.
Check r+n assimilation in gəmfašaṇṇo and the metal riṣaṣ against the edition; the edition translation 'tin' is retained verbatim.
Check ṣ in 75/45 mfaṣrola versus inherited mfašrola. Dissolving salt belongs here, not to fṣr dream interpretation, but no spelling correction is inferred.
Clarify hul dbaxi in MAC NE Story of Joseph/44: the English 'melted until he cried' has uncertain temporal relation and is not selected as a new example.
The historical split proposed in the inherited head cannot be determined from these occurrences alone.
Confirm whether mafšəriwo, mafšarle and kmafšərile reflect II vowel rearrangement or productive III; no new III is established.
At Jan 2.5/1574, verify fəšrinawo u šamʕo: transitive I, reduced II, or a missing element? The proposed I transitive sense is withheld.
At Jan 4.I/502, is fəšlina an assimilated fšr form or another root? This token is withheld from examples.
Is mfašarle i kefo at Jan 1.21/1046 a conventional expression for a moving speech or a one-off hyperbole? Only this attestation supports the proposed collocation.
Correct the dative adjective ending
rationale: Nach governs the dative; with der and feminine Kunst the adjective must be ärztlichen. The edition repeats the defective ending, but the agreement error is unambiguous.

summary: Correct lies → ließ
rationale: The sentence describes rendering fat and requires the past tense ließ, not the imperative lies. The edition at 29/155 reads “ließ es ... aus”.

summary: Correct agreement and case with Schale
rationale: Schale is feminine, and the rendering takes place in the bowl. The edition confirms “in einer kleinen Schale”.

summary: Restore r in the dative plural Dornsträuchern
rationale: The dative plural of Dornstrauch is Dornsträuchern. The edition at 29/155 also reads “mit Dornsträuchern”.

summary: Correct the plural article before Fässern
rationale: Fässern is dative plural, requiring den rather than singular der. The edition has “von den großen fässern”; preserve the glossary’s grossen spelling.

summary: Watered lime/aggregate loses its solid consistency. Retain under the widened dissolution gloss; the precise slaking process is unresolved and no literal thermal melting is inferred.
A miraculous stone-melting report is a material extension, not a new figurative sense.
Causative melting applies to butter, rendered tail fat, gold and silver, and dissolution to salt. Metal versus food does not establish a new sense.
A funeral speaker melts stone: record the attested expression as a collocation, not a separate general emotional-movement sense. One hyperbolic use does not establish conventional idiomatic status.
